claim: Young scientists taking on a faculty position quickly transition from being a team member to a team leader.
source: As young scientists taking on a faculty position, we quickly transition from being a team member to a team leader
evidence: This is a direct assertion about the experience of young scientists in faculty positions, based on the author's observations and experiences.

claim: Young scientists in faculty positions transition from never worrying about securing funding to being overwhelmed with grant deadlines.
source: from never worrying about securing funding to being overwhelmed with grant deadlines
evidence: This is a direct assertion about the changing responsibilities of young faculty members.

claim: Young faculty transition from managing a single project to planning and guiding the work and careers of several students and post-docs.
source: from managing a single project to planning and guiding the work and careers of several students and post-docs
evidence: This is a direct assertion about the expanded responsibilities of faculty members.

claim: Young faculty transition from worrying about themselves to being absorbed in worrying about everything except their wellness.
source: from worrying about ourselves to being absorbed in worrying about everything except our wellness
evidence: This is a direct assertion about the shift in priorities and concerns of new faculty members.

claim: The great majority of young faculty have never developed a course or taught classes on their own.
source: The great majority of us have never developed a course or taught classes on our own, yet we are all expected to assume these responsibilities.
evidence: This is a direct assertion about the teaching experience of new faculty members.

claim: All young faculty are expected to assume teaching responsibilities despite lack of prior experience.
source: The great majority of us have never developed a course or taught classes on our own, yet we are all expected to assume these responsibilities.
evidence: This is a direct assertion about institutional expectations for new faculty.

claim: Many universities give good support when it comes to teaching.
source: Many universities give good support when it comes to teaching
evidence: This is a direct assertion about university support systems.

claim: Most universities offer very little training or help in project and team management, leadership, mentoring and conflict resolution.

evidence: This is a direct assertion about the lack of institutional support in specific areas.

claim: Most universities offer very little training or help in mental health awareness and intervention.

claim: Faculty are expected to learn everything on the job.
source: We are expected to learn everything on the job.
evidence: This is a direct assertion about the learning expectations for faculty.

claim: Faculty learn by making mistakes that they and their students and staff directly or indirectly end up paying for.
source: In other words, we learn by making mistakes that we – and to some extent our students and staff – directly or indirectly end up paying for.
evidence: This is a direct assertion about the consequences of on-the-job learning for faculty.

claim: As the tenure clock starts ticking, stress and anxiety often begin to increase.
source: As the tenure clock starts ticking, stress and anxiety often begin to increase
evidence: This is a direct assertion about the psychological impact of the tenure process.

claim: The stakes become higher during the tenure period.
source: the stakes become higher
evidence: This is a direct assertion about the increasing pressure during the tenure period.

claim: Many faculty begin to struggle with the ambiguity of the tenure criteria.
source: many begin to struggle with the ambiguity of the tenure criteria and the lack of feedback
evidence: This is a direct assertion about challenges faculty face during the tenure process.

claim: Many faculty struggle with the lack of feedback during the tenure process.
source: many begin to struggle with the ambiguity of the tenure criteria and the lack of feedback
evidence: This is a direct assertion about the lack of feedback during tenure.

claim: The pressure mounts to publish papers in 'high impact journals' during the tenure period.
source: The pressure mounts to publish papers in 'high impact journals', to secure prestigious grants, go on lecture tours, and fill in all the blanks in our CV.
evidence: This is a direct assertion about the pressures faced by faculty seeking tenure.

claim: Frustration, disappointment, self-doubt or burnout are all too common throughout the faculty journey.
source: Frustration, disappointment, self-doubt or burnout are all too common throughout this journey.
evidence: This is a direct assertion about the mental health challenges faced by faculty.

claim: Even after tenure, the pressure often does not go away.
source: Even after tenure, the pressure often does not go away.
evidence: This is a direct assertion about the continuation of pressure after achieving tenure.

claim: After tenure, faculty transition from one type of stress to another.
source: Instead, we simply transition from one type of stress to another: from being anxious about publishing and securing tenure to being worried about funding, deadlines, increased administrative duties, the pressure to secure more prestigious grants and awards, and concerns for our reputation.
evidence: This is a direct assertion about the changing nature of stress after tenure.

claim: The hypercompetitive academic culture has ways of always keeping faculty on their toes.
source: The hypercompetitive academic culture has ways of always keeping you on your toes.
evidence: This is a direct assertion about the nature of academic culture.

claim: For senior faculty, the definition of success is a constantly moving target that is shaped and reshaped by the achievements of peers and the expectations of superiors.
source: For senior faculty, the definition of success is a constantly moving target that is shaped and reshaped by the achievements of our peers and the expectations of our superiors.
evidence: This is a direct assertion about how success is defined for senior faculty.

claim: After achieving tenure, success becomes much harder to define.
source: After achieving tenure, success becomes much harder to define, especially because the more senior we get, the less feedback we receive.
evidence: This is a direct assertion about the difficulty of defining success post-tenure.

claim: The more senior faculty get, the less feedback they receive.
source: especially because the more senior we get, the less feedback we receive
evidence: This is a direct assertion about the relationship between seniority and feedback.

claim: There is a lack of acknowledgement that faculty may be struggling.

evidence: This is a direct assertion about institutional awareness of faculty struggles.

claim: There is an absence of formal or informal support from institutions for struggling faculty.

claim: Academia is not the place where faculty are likely to get second chances.

claim: Peers may view faculty failure less as a potential learning experience and more as a sign that they are not fit for academia.
source: Our peers may view our failure less as a potential learning experience and more as a sign that we are not fit for academia.
